```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```


## Convert the annual Core files

HCUP distributes the Core file as fixed-width ASCII. Unpack the annual
archive and pass the `.asc` file to `nis_convert(path, dir)`. Repeat for each
data year using the same private output directory. The supported ASCII
layouts use the annual Core filenames and fields. The 2015 ASCII Core file
has separate diagnosis and procedure files. Prepare those separately
before an analysis that needs the code slots.

For Stata (`.dta`), SAS (`.sas7bdat`), or SPSS (`.sav`), the call is the
same. This example converts a Stata file made from invented data.

```{r convert}
source <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |> collect()
stata <- file.path(tempdir(), "NIS_2019_Core.dta")
haven::write_dta(source, stata)
annual <- tempfile("nis-annual-")
dir.create(annual)
nis_convert(stata, annual)
```

If conversion reports malformed UTF-8, check the source encoding and
correct the source or supply its known encoding for a haven format.
For example, use `encoding = "latin1"` for confirmed Latin-1 input. An
encoding override cannot repair damaged bytes.

## Open the years you need

```{r open}
nis <- nis_open(annual, years = 2019, check_release = FALSE)
analysis <- nis |> select(nis_vars_design(), AGE, LOS)
colnames(analysis)
nis |> count(YEAR) |> collect()
```

`nis_open()` returns a DuckDB query. Keep the annual release check on when using
complete licensed releases. Compare
the release-check warnings with the annual file documentation. Use
`check_release = FALSE` for an intentional extract.
Keep projection, flags, and other supported operations before
`collect()`. [How easyNIS works](how-easynis-works.html)

## Check that your code fields can be read

```{r check-codes}
nis |> count(I10_DX1, sort = TRUE) |> head(5) |> collect()
nis |> count(I10_PR1, sort = TRUE) |> head(5) |> collect()
```

A query can open before DuckDB reads text from the code fields. Check
the diagnosis and procedure columns used in your study. If one fails
with malformed UTF-8, reconvert from the correctly encoded source into
a new directory and review the release check.

## Join companion files

```{r existing-fields}
needed <- c("HOSP_BEDSIZE", "HOSP_LOCTEACH")
missing <- setdiff(needed, colnames(nis))
missing
```

If the result is empty, the requested fields are already in the
opened extract. Check their source and data years and use the existing
fields. Join only missing fields from a separate companion path.

Prepare annual companion Parquet files with their documented keys.
Use `nis_join_companion(nis, hospital_path, component = "hospital",
columns = all_of(missing))` to add hospital characteristics. Use
`component = "severity"` with the Severity file. Select only fields you
need and check coverage after joining.

`TOTAL_DISC` in the Hospital file counts sampled discharges. The join
helper rejects that field. Use weighted discharge estimates for national
totals. [Years and coding eras](years-and-eras.html)
